newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 20 bps to 11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 20 bps to 11.5 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 20 basis points to 11.5 percent despite an abundant supply of kuna funds, dealers said.
Friday's trade totalled 25.4 million kuna, up from Thursday's 12.3 million, leaving a 79.6 million surplus on the supply side.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 16.5 million kuna, most of which was call money granted at 11 percent.
Term rates ranged between 10 percent for one-week and 15 percent for two-week loans.
Insurers rolled over 8.9 million kuna at 10 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and Monday firmer at 5.8345 against the dollar and 3.5605 to the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
